0:00-0:25
Show homepage cooling animation.
A persuasive PDE animation does not tell us whether a computation is resolved. PhaseAtlas connects an editable model to visual experiments, numerical checks and an exportable research record. I am Niu Te from Imperial College London.

0:25-0:55
Show Robin model and refinement chart.
A hot rod exchanging heat with its surroundings gives a practical starting point. Robin boundary data represent wall exchange. A separate exact heat-equation mode lets us test the numerical implementation: on sixteen, thirty-two and sixty-four cells, errors decrease with observed order approximately two. A balance audit exposes the relationship between heat leaving the walls and thermal-content change.

0:55-1:25
Show parameter map and original wave animation.
Every cell in a parameter map retains its trajectory and metric definition. A researcher can compare cooling responses and revisit a failed run. The original fourth-order front from my earlier research adds wave-motion and deformation diagnostics, with configurable extra boundary conditions in the general Studio. The numerical evidence is not presented as a stability theorem.

1:25-1:55
Show JSON export and article.
Another researcher receives equations, boundaries, arrays and method information, plus selected independent Python checks. The current suite passes ninety tests. The implementation is independent and AI-assisted; simulation runs locally without a runtime language-model API. The dated package separates prior work from contributions made during the event. PhaseAtlas helps turn an interesting picture into an experiment that someone else can inspect.
